newsitem.title: USA: Most US debt futures steady at close of pit trade.
newsitem.headline: Most US debt futures steady at close of pit trade.

text.p: Most U.S. debt futures were steady at the close of pit trade, with March T-bonds and June Eurodollars locked in tight ranges ahead of the second leg of the Treasury's quarterly refunding, traders said.
March T-bonds nudged to 112-12/32 after the results of the Treasury's $17.75 billion three-year note auction were released on Tuesday afternoon.
"Dealers might have owned a little too much," one bond futures trader said.
"It looked like the street owned a little more than they would have liked," another bond futures source said.
However, activity remained extremely light in the afternoon, with locals as the primary participants jostling around prices in the pits.

One major U.S. firm continued to sell spotty amounts of March T-bonds, while another U.S. house was reportedly accumulating contracts through the 112-20/32 level only to dump them after the auction, they said.

The Treasury's three-year note auction produced an average yield of 5.997 percent, in-line with most traders' estimates, but several floor sources said the bid-to-cover and noncomp bids were a little on the low side.
"It's certainly not bearish, but just nothing to get excited about," one futures trader said. "I really see no surprises out of the three-year note auction."
Some traders said New York Federal Reserve president William McDonough's comments late in the day had as much as do with the March bond contract's slim decline, as the auction results.

McDonough, speaking to investment analysts in Dublin, Ireland, said the U.S. economy was operating fairly close to full capacity, and that low inflation in the U.S. does not rule out potential price shocks.
The market showed little reaction to U.S. Treasury secretary Robert Rubin's comments that the dollar's fall has now corrected itself to a normal mode.

At the outset of pit trade, several traders expressed caution ahead of Rubin's testimony to Congress. They were looking for Rubin to elaborate on the U.S. administration's dollar policy after the G7 meeting on Saturday. Rubin was testifying about the 1998 federal budget to Congress.
The 2.5-percent rise in the Redbook Retail Sales Index for the first week of February also failed to spark activity in either the bond or Eurodollar futures floor.

At the end of pit trade, March T-bonds were unchanged at 112-15/32, 10-year notes were off 01/32 at 109-16/32, June and September Eurodollars once again ended the day unchanged at 94.35 and 94.22, respectively, June T-bills were also steady at 94.89 and March munibonds were up 03/32 at 116-04/32.
